title: Hasten to the remembrance
hookLine: when the call is made on Friday, hasten to remember Allah and leave trade (62:9)

cards: Friday, a little after noon, in a busy city. A shopkeeper pulls the shutter halfway down and hangs a sign. A taxi driver parks two streets away.
Office workers drift out of glass towers in twos and threes, some still on their phones. A boy runs because he's late. They're all heading the same way, toward the sound of the call.
For about an hour, buying and selling stops. Surah sixty-two, Al-Jumu'ah, is where that hour comes from.

teach.b: Verse nine. Pickthall: "O ye who believe! When the call is heard for the prayer of the day of congregation, haste unto remembrance of Allah and leave your trading."

The day of congregation is yawm al-jumu'ah, from the root j-m-', to gather. Friday is literally gathering day. That day the noon prayer is replaced by a sermon, the khutbah, and two units of prayer, prayed together.
The verb for hasten is fas'aw. Does it mean run? Commentators said no.
Bukhari records that the Prophet ﷺ told people not to rush to the prayer but to walk with calm and dignity, even if they'd miss part of it.
So fas'aw means set out with purpose, not sprint. And leave your trading is concrete: when the call comes, the deal can wait. Hadith fill in the morning before.

teach.h: COME EARLY: A CAMEL, THEN AN EGG.
teach.b: Bukhari records that whoever bathes on Friday and goes early to the prayer is like one who offered a camel; a little later, a cow; then a ram, a hen, an egg.
And when the imam comes out to give the sermon, the angels close their records and sit down to listen. Who must attend?
Most jurists say adult men who are resident and able; women may attend and many do, and for travelers and the sick it's lifted. The verse ends: that is better for you, if you only knew.
One hour of the week, cut out of the market and handed back to remembrance.

how: On Fridays, many Muslims bathe, wear clean clothes, and go to the mosque for the congregational prayer, which has a sermon and two units of prayer in place of the noon prayer; most jurists hold it obligatory for adult, resident men, and women may attend.

practice: Think of the next thing you're due at: a prayer, a meeting, a class, a meal with someone. Picture yourself arriving ten minutes early, walking calmly, and sitting settled in the room before anyone else, ready to listen.
Let your breath slow to that pace now.

wordCard.voice: Khutbah, the sermon that comes with the Friday prayer, when Surah Al-Jumu'ah says to leave trade and hasten to the remembrance of God. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: so set out for the remembrance of God. sa'y, the root of fas'aw, means effort, going with purpose.

carryVoice: Your line: leave trade for a while. One hour a week belongs to the gathering. See you next time.
